---
title: "Dialysis facility density and early dialysis initiation: a revised analysis"
format: html
---

## The study

Hemmige and colleagues studied 844,466 adults who started in-center hemodialysis in the United States from 2011 to 2019, using the US Renal Data System (USRDS) [@hemmige2024density]. Patients living in the Hospital Service Areas (HSAs, which the paper calls health service areas) with the most dialysis facilities per resident had higher odds of starting dialysis at an estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) above 10 mL/min/1.73 m²: an odds ratio of 1.06 (95% CI 1.02 to 1.10) compared with HSAs with no facility. The difference is small: in the paper's linear models, patients in the densest HSAs started at an eGFR about 0.1 mL/min/1.73 m² higher (eTable 3). The odds rose across the density categories and were clearest in the densest; the comparison group, HSAs with no facility, held about 4% of the patients. In models fitted separately by race, the fully adjusted estimate was the same in White and Black patients (odds ratio 1.05), but statistically significant only in White patients (95% CI 1.00 to 1.10, against 0.93 to 1.18 in the smaller group of Black patients; eTable 1) [@hemmige2024density]. The [clinical background](quarto/background.qmd) page explains why the question matters.

## What this site does

This repository rebuilds the paper's analysis from public code, as a revised analysis rather than a replication of its numbers. The original analysis was a single R Markdown file of more than 3,000 lines (shown [here](quarto/original.qmd), with local file locations removed). It is rebuilt with packages that do the repetitive work:

-   **usRds** [@usrds_pkg] loads and labels the USRDS files, and attaches CMS dialysis facility counts to each patient by the date dialysis started.
-   **flowchart** [@flowchart_pkg] applies every exclusion and counts it at the same time, so the cohort diagram is the cohort.
-   **tidycensus** [@tidycensus] downloads the American Community Survey, and every other area-level file is downloaded from its publisher.

Rebuilding the analysis this way turned up several errors in the original code. They are corrected here, and each one is listed, with what it can change, on the [differences page](quarto/differences.qmd). Where the original code and the paper disagree, the choice is left to the investigators.

## Methods

The authoritative specification is [`analysis-plan.md`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Dialysis-facility-density-USRDS/blob/main/analysis-plan.md). In brief: incident adults on in-center hemodialysis with an eGFR of 20 or below; exposure, HSA dialysis facilities per 100,000 residents in five categories; outcome, eGFR of 10 or above at initiation; mixed-effects logistic models with a random intercept for HSA, progressively adjusted for patient, clinical, area and HSA characteristics. Reporting follows STROBE [@vonelm2007strobe], as in the paper, and RECORD [@benchimol2015record], added for this analysis.

## Status

The code is complete and tested on synthetic data. It has not yet been run on the USRDS data, so this site shows code and methods only; no results from USRDS data are published here. Its results are not expected to match the published ones exactly: the processing now runs through `usRds`, which is still being developed, public files are re-downloaded, and errors in the original code are corrected. The site will be revised as the package develops. Open decisions are listed on the [differences page](quarto/differences.qmd#open-decisions) and tracked as [GitHub issues](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Dialysis-facility-density-USRDS/issues).

The analysis also serves as a demonstration of how an analysis like this can be rebuilt with current tools. Where neither the paper nor the original code settles a choice, a few were made for the demonstration rather than by a full scientific review: the rule accepting a cause-of-kidney-failure code when two of three language models agree, and the grouping of race into the paper's five groups. They affect the Table 1 cause and race rows, the covariates of Models 1 to 3, and the race-stratified eTables. Each is marked "chosen for this demonstration" where it is described.
